# DORA Art. 30 contract checklist

<!-- Generated by `python -m dora_roi.docs`; do not edit by hand. -->

Key contractual provisions of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, Art. 30, as assessed by `roi contracts` and the *Contracts* screen of the workbench. Art. 30(2) applies to every contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services; Art. 30(3) applies in addition to arrangements on ICT services supporting critical or important functions. The wording paraphrases the regulation – see [ASSUMPTIONS.md](ASSUMPTIONS.md) (A-A30-*).

**22 provisions** (12 for all ICT services, 10 additionally for critical or important functions). ★ = key provision (listed first within a priority).

## Art. 30(1) – form of the contract

| ID | Reference | Provision | Requirement | Related RoI fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `30.1` | DORA Art. 30(1) | Written contract in one document, including the SLAs | Rights and obligations of both parties are clearly allocated and set out in writing; the full contract, including the service level agreements, is documented in one written document available on paper or in a downloadable, durable and accessible format. | — |

## Art. 30(2) – all contractual arrangements

| ID | Reference | Provision | Requirement | Related RoI fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `30.2.a.1` | DORA Art. 30(2)(a) | Description of all functions and ICT services | A clear and complete description of all functions and ICT services to be provided by the ICT third-party service provider. | B_02.02 c0060 |
| `30.2.a.2` | DORA Art. 30(2)(a) | ★ Subcontracting: whether permitted and under which conditions | The contract states whether subcontracting of an ICT service supporting a critical or important function, or material parts of it, is permitted and, if so, the conditions that apply to such subcontracting. *Related: DORA Art. 30(5); RTS on subcontracting (Art. 30(5)).* | B_05.02 |
| `30.2.b.1` | DORA Art. 30(2)(b) | Locations of service provision and of data processing and storage | The regions or countries where the contracted or subcontracted functions and ICT services are provided and where data is processed, including the storage location. | B_02.02 c0130, B_02.02 c0150, B_02.02 c0160 |
| `30.2.b.2` | DORA Art. 30(2)(b) | Advance notice before changing locations | The ICT third-party service provider must notify the financial entity in advance if it envisages changing the locations of service provision or data processing. | — |
| `30.2.c` | DORA Art. 30(2)(c) | Availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality of data | Provisions on availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality in relation to the protection of data, including personal data. | B_02.02 c0170 |
| `30.2.d` | DORA Art. 30(2)(d) | ★ Access, recovery and return of data on insolvency, resolution or termination | Access, recovery and return, in an easily accessible format, of personal and non-personal data processed for the financial entity in the event of the provider's insolvency, resolution or discontinuation of business, or termination of the contract. | — |
| `30.2.e` | DORA Art. 30(2)(e) | Service level descriptions, including updates and revisions | Service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof. | — |
| `30.2.f` | DORA Art. 30(2)(f) | Assistance in ICT incidents at no additional or a pre-agreed cost | The provider must assist the financial entity when an ICT incident related to the service occurs, at no additional cost or at a cost determined ex ante. | — |
| `30.2.g` | DORA Art. 30(2)(g) | ★ Full cooperation with competent and resolution authorities | The provider must fully cooperate with the competent authorities and the resolution authorities of the financial entity, including persons appointed by them. | — |
| `30.2.h` | DORA Art. 30(2)(h) | ★ Termination rights and minimum notice periods | Termination rights and related minimum notice periods, in line with the expectations of competent and resolution authorities; the termination circumstances of DORA Art. 28(7) must be covered. *Related: DORA Art. 28(7).* | B_02.02 c0100, B_02.02 c0110 |
| `30.2.i` | DORA Art. 30(2)(i) | Participation in ICT security awareness and resilience training | Conditions for the provider's participation in the financial entity's ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training (Art. 13(6)). *Related: DORA Art. 13(6).* | — |

## Art. 30(3) – ICT services supporting critical or important functions

| ID | Reference | Provision | Requirement | Related RoI fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `30.3.a` | DORA Art. 30(3)(a) | Full service levels with precise quantitative and qualitative targets | Full service level descriptions with precise quantitative and qualitative performance targets, allowing effective monitoring and appropriate corrective action without undue delay when service levels are not met. | B_06.01 c0080, B_06.01 c0090 |
| `30.3.b` | DORA Art. 30(3)(b) | Notice periods and reporting obligations, incl. material developments | Notice periods and reporting obligations of the provider, including notification of any development that might materially impact its ability to provide the services effectively and in line with agreed service levels. | — |
| `30.3.c` | DORA Art. 30(3)(c) | Tested business contingency plans and appropriate ICT security | The provider implements and tests business contingency plans and has ICT security measures, tools and policies providing an appropriate level of security in line with the financial entity's regulatory framework. | — |
| `30.3.d` | DORA Art. 30(3)(d) | ★ Participation and full cooperation in threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) | The provider must participate and fully cooperate in the financial entity's threat-led penetration testing under Art. 26 and 27. *Related: DORA Art. 26; DORA Art. 27.* | — |
| `30.3.e.i` | DORA Art. 30(3)(e)(i) | ★ Unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit | Unrestricted rights of access, inspection and audit by the financial entity, an appointed third party and the competent authority, including the right to take copies of relevant documentation on site, not impeded by other contractual arrangements or policies. *Related: DORA Art. 28(6).* | B_07.01 c0070 |
| `30.3.e.ii` | DORA Art. 30(3)(e)(ii) | Right to agree alternative assurance levels | The right to agree on alternative assurance levels if other clients' rights are affected. | — |
| `30.3.e.iii` | DORA Art. 30(3)(e)(iii) | Full cooperation during on-site inspections and audits | The provider must fully cooperate during on-site inspections and audits by the competent authorities, the Lead Overseer, the financial entity or an appointed third party. | — |
| `30.3.e.iv` | DORA Art. 30(3)(e)(iv) | Scope, procedures and frequency of inspections and audits | The obligation to provide details on the scope, procedures to be followed and frequency of such inspections and audits. | — |
| `30.3.f.i` | DORA Art. 30(3)(f)(i) | ★ Exit strategy: mandatory adequate transition period | Exit strategies, in particular a mandatory adequate transition period during which the provider continues providing the functions or ICT services, to reduce the risk of disruption or ensure effective resolution and restructuring. *Related: DORA Art. 28(8).* | B_07.01 c0080 |
| `30.3.f.ii` | DORA Art. 30(3)(f)(ii) | Exit strategy: migration to another provider or in-house | The transition period allows the financial entity to migrate to another ICT third-party service provider or to in-house solutions, consistent with the complexity of the service. *Related: DORA Art. 28(8).* | B_07.01 c0090, B_07.01 c0110 |
